newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: British yachtswoman in southern ocean rescue.
newsitem.headline: British yachtswoman in southern ocean rescue.

text.p: A 27-year-old Welsh woman taking part in the world's toughest yacht race was winched to safety in rough seas off the Falkand Islands on Sunday after complaining of severe abdominal pains.

Rhian Jenkins from Swansea, Wales was part of the crew of the yacht Global Teamwork, taking part in the BT Global Challenge race in which competitors sail the "wrong way" around the world -- against the winds and currents.

Rather than risk the fearsome seas of Cape Horn with an ill crew member, skipper Mervin Owen decided to ask Britain's Royal Air Force based in the Falkland Islands to send a helicopter to the yacht about 100 miles from the South Atlantic islands.
Jenkins was winched up and taken to hospital in the Falkland Islands in a three-hour rescue mission.
Speaking from her hospital bed, she said: "I hope to rejoin the race in Wellington (New Zealand) if the doctors here can find out what is wrong."

The BT Global Challenge is being contested by 14 identical yachts which left Southampton, England in September. They will go on to New Zealand, Australia and the United States before returning to Southampton next July.
